title: The Portrait of Old Chapel Road
premise: Folklorist Ivo Yarrow arrives in the half-abandoned village of Hollowmere to record its dying songs, keeping careful distance from neighbors who count her doors and dim their lamps when she passes. Her overnight field recordings begin capturing a second voice—dry, patient, answering questions she never asked aloud—and she learns it belongs to something beneath the old chapel well, a thing the village founders bound with a ritual they never finished. As the well refills and villagers who once ignored her start dying or vanishing, Ivo discovers the founders' pact required an outsider's voice to complete, which is why they let her stay invisible: she was always meant to be the final instrument. In the flooded crypt beneath Old Chapel Road, Ivo must choose between finishing the ritual as written—which demands she surrender her own voice forever—or rewriting it with the found family she never expected, sealing the well at the cost of the village itself.
about_author: Sable Vasquez is the pen name of a former archivist who spent three years cataloguing oral histories in remote coastal villages before turning to fiction. They write horror about quiet places, borrowed voices, and the debts communities owe to strangers.

chapters.title: The House That Counts Back
chapters.summary: Ivo Yarrow's POV. She arrives in Hollowmere at dusk, renting the last habitable cottage on Old Chapel Road, and immediately notices the villagers' habits: doors counted aloud, lamps shuttered at nine, no one singing past dark. Emotional beat: wary self-containment—Ivo has spent her life being unremarkable on purpose, and Hollowmere seems to agree she should be.

chapters.title: Songs Nobody Sings Twice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the village pub she records old Tam Weller singing a harvest lament; mid-verse he stops, goes grey, and refuses to repeat a single line, though his own daughter begs him. The landlady quietly refunds Ivo's drink. Emotional beat: first crack of unease—the archive she came for is guarded by fear, not indifference.

chapters.title: Field Notes, Night One
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, alone. Reviewing her first night of ambient recordings, she hears beneath the wind a second voice—low, cracked, patient—answering questions in the pauses between her own breaths. She tells herself it's radio bleed. Emotional beat: the scholar's thrill curdling into dread; she plays it eleven times.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The dry chapel well, sealed since 1911, is found brimming with black water; children are kept indoors and the vicar burns something sweet-smelling at its lip. Ivo photographs it and finds the water level higher in every frame than in memory. Emotional beat: the village's fear becomes contagious; her invisibility starts to feel like surveillance.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Maren Oduya, the only villager who speaks to her openly—a beekeeper whose family arrived after the founding—brings honey and warns her: 'They're kind to you because you're temporary.' Ivo, starved for warmth, lets her in. Emotional beat: first genuine connection, shadowed by Maren's warning that kindness here has a ledger.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with archival interludes. In the chapel vestry she finds the founders' ledger: a ritual in seven verses, six signed in blood, the seventh line blank. The final verse requires 'a voice from outside the blood.' Emotional beat: cold recognition—her arrival was not coincidence but invitation, decades deferred.

chapters.title: Questions She Never Asked
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The night voice grows specific, reciting details of Ivo's childhood she never recorded, then asks: 'Will you sing the seventh?' She answers nothing, but the recorder captures her heartbeat accelerating like an answer. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo—the thing knows her better than anyone alive.

chapters.title: What Happened to Ellery Finch
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ivo and Maren. A young man who mocked the customs walks the road at midnight singing the harvest lament; by morning his voice is gone entirely and he weeps without sound. The village closes ranks around him. Emotional beat: grief and guilt—Ivo realizes her recordings may have taught him the song.

chapters.title: The Pact Explained Badly
chapters.summary: Tam Weller's POV. Drunk and terrified, Tam finally explains: the founders drowned something in the well that grants harvests in exchange for songs; the ritual keeps it sleeping, renewed each generation by a sung seventh verse. It has been forty years. Emotional beat: confession as betrayal—he tells Ivo because telling her makes her complicit.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She wakes to find chalk tallies on her doorframe—one for every night she's slept there—and understands the villagers have been counting toward something. Maren admits the tally marks the nights until the well crests its stone rim. Emotional beat: the found-family warmth fractures; belonging was always arithmetic here.

chapters.title: Running Water
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She tries to leave; the road out loops back to Old Chapel Road no matter which direction she drives, and her phone holds one bar of signal that only plays her own recordings back. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair—the village isn't trapping her; the thing under the well is.

chapters.title: The Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, dream sequence bleeding into waking. She dreams of standing in the flooded crypt among the founders' skeletons, all of them mouthless, all of them singing through her. She wakes with salt water in her lungs and a melody in her head she cannot stop humming. Emotional beat: bodily invasion—the ritual has begun choosing her.

chapters.title: Six Signatures
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren researches her own late husband's family and finds his name was meant to be the seventh signer; he died before the rite, leaving the village exposed. She brings this to Ivo not as warning but as plea. Emotional beat: two outsiders forging real trust inside a lie both were told.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vicar Ansel Crane's POV. He offers Ivo sanctuary, protection, even love, if she sings the seventh verse willingly—insisting it is mercy, since the thing will take her voice either way. Emotional beat: seductive reasonableness; the villain believes himself a shepherd, and nearly convinces her.

chapters.title: Ellery's Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Voiceless Ellery writes her a note: 'It doesn't want your song. It wants your consent. Don't give it kindly.' Ivo realizes the ritual's cruelty is designed to make surrender feel like grace. Emotional beat: clarity through another's ruin; loyalty to the village and truth about the village split apart.

chapters.title: Nineteen Tallies
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. With three nights left, Ivo and Maren decode the ledger's marginalia: the founders left a flaw on purpose—an eighth verse, unwritten, that could bind the well permanently but requires the singers to mean it, together, as chosen family rather than sacrifice. Emotional beat: hope with teeth—a way out that costs more than obedience.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in short sections. The village prepares: some pray for Ivo's compliance, some plan to force her, Tam drinks, Ellery stands guard outside her door with a bell. Emotional beat: dread and tenderness braided—the whole cast holding its breath on the eve of the well cresting.

chapters.title: Descent, Old Chapel Road
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The well overflows; black water runs down the road singing in six dead voices. Ivo, Maren, and Ellery descend into the crypt through the collapsing chapel floor while the vicar follows, meaning to complete the founders' version. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve—she goes down singing, badly, on purpose.

chapters.title: The Seventh Verse
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax part one. In the crypt the thing wears the faces of everyone Ivo has lost, offering her a place where she'd finally belong if she only finishes the song alone. The vicar begins the sixth verse to force her hand. Emotional beat: the temptation of easy belonging versus the harder truth that belonging can't be bought with silence.

chapters.title: An Eighth Verse, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Climax part two, ensemble POV. Maren and Ellery arrive bleeding, and instead of the seventh verse the three sing the improvised eighth—off-key, human, meaning every word—while the vicar's forced verse tears him apart for singing falsely. The well convulses. Emotional beat: triumphant defiance; the monster cannot digest a song given freely by people who chose each other.

chapters.title: What the Water Left
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The well drains to clean, still water; the founders' bones rest; the tally marks wash from her door. But Ivo's singing voice is gone—not taken, spent—and the village must learn to live without the bargain's bounty. Emotional beat: exhausted peace; loss that feels like payment made rather than theft endured.

chapters.title: A Song Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. Months later, Ivo stays in Hollowmere by choice, teaching the children the harvest lament so it can finally be sung twice safely. On the last page, someone new knocks at her door—a folklorist, passing through—and Ivo counts her own doors, smiles, and leaves the lamp lit. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the outsider becomes the keeper, and the story ends where it began, changed.
